note: Recast from the original description of the new species by Maiti & Chakraborty (1994), the original in English; the alate is recorded as Unknown in the original. Large soldier, small soldier and worker are described, and the measurement tables are transcribed (large soldier: holotype value and range of 10 individuals; small soldier and worker: range of 10 individuals). Of the worker measurements only body length is entered, because the remaining columns of the original table run across a page break and were not fully captured by the OCR.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Large soldier: head capsule, postclypeus and thorax yellowish brown, the frons slightly paler; mandibles blackish brown at the tip and yellowish brown at the base; antennae, labrum, legs and abdomen pale yellow; anteclypeus translucent, labrum with a whitish tinge. Head sparsely covered with short hairs; pronotum with few hairs, mostly on the margins; abdomen more densely hairy. Body length (excluding the antennae) 6.10—6.45 mm. Head capsule somewhat quadrate, length almost equal to width; lateral margins nearly straight, slightly constricted at the antennal fossae and then clearly narrowing anteriorly; posterolateral corners and posterior margin broadly rounded. Fontanelle round and distinct, situated a little below the frontoclypeal suture (0.20 mm from it); the frons bears a narrow shallow groove running from the fontanelle to the tip of the labrum, widest and clearest at the frontoclypeal suture. Eyes and ocelli absent. Antenna 16 segments: segments 1 and 2 almost hairless, the rest moderately hairy and increasingly so towards the tip; segment 3 long-conical, 1.5 times segment 2 or segment 4; from segment 5 to the penultimate segment nearly pyriform; the last segment oval and narrower than the others. Labrum subquadrate, slightly wider than long; anterior margin weakly bilobed, the fringe of small hairs extending laterally to near the anterior 1/3; a few erect hairs just below the anterolateral corners. Anteclypeus a narrow strip, translucent, much wider than long, hairless. Postclypeus transverse, hairy, weakly delimited from the frons; anterior margin curved outward, with a median fontanelle groove. Mandibles stout, strongly incurved at the tip (especially the right), widest at the base; left mandible with 2 prominent sharp marginal teeth close together, almost at the middle of the mandible; right mandible also with 2 marginal teeth, the first sharp and lateral, situated at the middle, the second small and blunt and far from the first, the inner margin deeply concave between the two. Postmentum rod-like, clearly shorter than the head; widest in the anterior 1/3, about 2 times the width of the narrowest part in the posterior 1/3; anterior margin nearly straight, posterior margin concave, with a few short hairs on the anterior half. Pronotum flat, the anterior lobe very weakly raised, width slightly less than 2 times the length and more than half the head width; anterior margin weakly curved outward, without a median notch; anterolateral corners narrowly rounded, posterolateral corners broadly rounded; posterior margin very weakly concave. Mesonotum equal to or slightly narrower than the pronotum, lateral margins broadly rounded; metanotum short and wider than the other nota, lateral margins broadly rounded, posterior margin with a weak median concavity. Legs hairy, femora slender; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate, the posterior part of the sternites with 1—2 rows of short stout hairs; cerci 2-segmented and hairy, styli 1-segmented. Large soldier measurements (mm, holotype/range of 10 individuals): head length to the mandibular bases 2.00/1.98—2.08; head width at the posterolateral ends of the antennal carinae 1.76/1.76—1.88; maximum head width 2.00/1.98—2.08; head height 1.19/1.19—1.25; left mandible length 1.08/1.08—1.10; distance from the first marginal tooth of the left mandible to the apical tooth 0.43/0.40—0.48; labrum length 0.53/0.53—0.58; labrum width 0.58/0.58—0.63; postmentum length 1.30/1.30—1.38; maximum postmentum width 0.53/0.53—0.56; minimum postmentum width 0.26/0.26—0.28; pronotum length 0.68/0.63—0.68; pronotum width 1.14/1.14—1.20; mesonotum width 1.09/1.09—1.14; metanotum width 1.22/1.22—1.29; antenna 16 segments.

Small soldier: head capsule, labrum, postclypeus, thorax and abdomen pale yellow; mandibles yellowish brown at the base and blackish brown at the tip; anteclypeus translucent white. Head with a few scattered short hairs; pronotum with hairs mostly on the margins, abdomen with long and short hairs. Body length 3.45—3.55 mm. Head capsule somewhat suboval, longer than wide, widest at the level of the antennal fossae, narrowing posteriorly into a rounded posterior margin. Fontanelle small and round, situated a little below the frontoclypeal suture (0.07 mm from it), opening backwards, with a narrow groove running from the frons to the tip of the labrum and widening anteriorly. Eyes and ocelli absent. Antenna 16 segments: segments 2 and 3 subequal, segment 4 the shortest; from segment 5 gradually thicker, the last segment slightly narrower. Labrum strongly rectangular, almost 2 times as wide as long, reaching the mandibular tips when closed; anterior margin strongly bilobed and translucent; anterolateral corners narrowly rounded, the fringe of fine hairs diminishing laterally; below the transparent margin a few pairs (3—4 pairs) of long erect hairs; longitudinal groove distinct. Anteclypeus transverse, a white strip, hairless. Postclypeus wider than long, hairy, with a median fontanelle groove. Mandibles slender, the tip very sharp; left mandible with 2 subequal marginal teeth directed forward, situated in the anterior 1/3; right mandible with 1 forward-directed and very sharp marginal tooth. Postmentum somewhat as in the large soldier but with the waist further back and the anterior narrow part also shorter; greatest width about 1.5 times the minimum width. Pronotum flat, wider than long, clearly narrower than the head; anterior margin with a blunt median projection; sides narrowing posteriorly; posterior margin weakly concave; short hairs mostly on the margins. Mesonotum wider than the pronotum, lateral margins rounded; metanotum much wider than the others, lateral margins narrowly rounded; legs and abdomen as in the large soldier. Small soldier measurements (mm, range of 10 individuals): head length to the mandibular bases 1.00—1.05; head width at the mandibular bases 0.63—0.68; head width at the posterolateral ends of the antennal carinae 0.92—0.95; maximum head width 0.88—0.92; head height 0.58—0.68; left mandible length 0.70—0.72; distance from the first marginal tooth to the apical tooth 0.14—0.15; labrum length 0.50—0.53; labrum width 0.24—0.28; postmentum length 0.72—0.74; maximum postmentum width 0.34—0.37; minimum postmentum width 0.24—0.26; pronotum length 0.43—0.48; pronotum width 0.65—0.68; mesonotum width 0.68—0.72; metanotum width 0.75—0.78; antenna 16 segments.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule, labrum and postclypeus straw yellow; mandibles pale yellow with dark brown tooth margins; antennae, thorax and abdomen paler than the head. Head and thorax sparsely hairy, the abdomen more hairy. Body length 5.38—5.75 mm. Head broadly quadrate, much wider than long; lateral margins weakly curved outward, posterior margin rounded. Fontanelle, eyes and ocelli absent. Antenna 17 segments: segments 2 and 3 subequal, segment 4 shorter than segment 3 and the shortest. Labrum dome-shaped, slightly wider than long, widest at the middle. Postclypeus large, hairy, weakly convex, divided into two halves by an incomplete median longitudinal line; anteclypeus narrow, translucent, hairless; mandibles of the Schedorhinotermes type. Pronotum saddle-shaped, much wider than long, the length slightly less than half the width; anterior margin strongly convex with a weak median notch; posterior margin straight. Legs slender, hairy; tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate and hairy; cerci 2-segmented, styli 1-segmented.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compared with translucens, bidentatus and tiwarii, which are similar in the morphology of the large soldier: this species is larger, head length 1.98—2.08 mm and width 1.98—2.08 mm (in translucens head length 1.59—1.85 and width 1.49—1.75 mm, and the head is slightly longer than wide); the second marginal tooth of the right mandible lies close to the first; the anterior margin of the labrum is weakly bilobed (nearly straight in translucens); the waist of the postmentum is strongly constricted (not noticeably constricted in translucens). Difference from bidentatus: the head narrows clearly anteriorly (nearly rectangular in bidentatus); the inner margin between the two marginal teeth of the right mandible is weakly concave (strongly concave in bidentatus); the pronotum width is clearly less than 2 times the length and clearly narrower than the head (almost 2 times the length in bidentatus). Difference from tiwarii: this species is larger and the head is strongly constricted anteriorly (head length 1.72—2.08 and width 1.63—2.08 mm; in tiwarii the head is subquadrate, head length 1.68—1.85 and width 1.60—1.68 mm); the right mandible has 2 distinct marginal teeth (only 1 in tiwarii); the postmental waist is about half the greatest width (about 2/3 in tiwarii). Type locality Nancowry, Nicobar Islands; known only from the type locality.
